subtitle: Seven business questions answered from 556 daily charts, with the statistics behind each answer. Full method: docs/insights.md.

questions.question: How long do songs survive on the Global Top 50?
questions.headline: 6 days
questions.answer: That is the median chart life. 53% of songs last a week or less, and the longest-charting 10% of songs hold 57% of all chart slots: the chart is a few long runs and many brief visits.
questions.evidence: 747 songs with a known debut · q1_longevity_distribution.sql

questions.question: Does a big debut mean a long run?
questions.headline: 10x longer
questions.answer: Songs that keep climbing after their debut chart a median 31 days in their first 180, against 3 for songs that peak on day one (64% of songs). Debut position itself is a weak predictor (Spearman ρ = -0.17), and collaborations last no longer than solo songs (6 vs 6 days, p = 0.96).
questions.evidence: Mann-Whitney U p < 0.001, effect size 0.69 · 571 songs with a full 180-day window

questions.question: Who owns the most chart real estate?
questions.answer: Taylor Swift held 6.7% of every chart slot, 2.1x the next artist. The top 10 artists hold 27% of the chart, with collaborations split fairly between credited artists.

questions.question: What happens when a superstar drops an album?
questions.headline: 30 of 50
questions.answer: On 21 Apr 2024, Taylor Swift held 30 of the 50 chart slots (HHI 3,669 against a typical 309). All 5 takeovers were album releases, and each faded within about a week.
questions.evidence: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of daily artist share · q4_album_takeovers.sql

questions.question: How seasonal is the chart?
questions.answer: Holiday songs, mostly decades old, took 94% of the chart on 26 Dec 2023, then fell to 4% on 28 Dec. December needs its own baseline in any trend analysis.

questions.question: When do new songs come out, and when do they chart?
questions.answer: 66% of new releases come out on a Friday (New Music Friday) and 76% debut on a Saturday or Sunday chart, a median 2 days after release. A song's chart fate is largely set within its first weekend.
questions.evidence: New releases with exact release dates · q8_release_weekday.sql

questions.question: Which songs ruled the #1 spot?
questions.headline: 77 days
questions.answer: Die With A Smile (Lady Gaga) held #1 longest, 57 days in a row. 37 songs reached #1; Seven (feat. Latto) (Explicit Ver.) got 75 days across 10 separate runs.
